meta.title: Biomimetic design and integrated biofabrication of an in-vitro three-dimensional multi-scale multilayer cortical model.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A six-layer brain-cortex-like model was built by combining extrusion printing of GelMA/fibrin with melt electrowritten fibres that run through all layers. The fibres guided neurite growth, and glial layers drew PC12 cells toward them.

formulations.crosslinking: UV (15 s) then CaCl2 0.2% + thrombin 10 U/mL
formulations.stiffness_note: 5% GelMA alone 8.48 kPa; fibrin lowers modulus (1.67 kPa at 1.5%)
formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 320 mbar. Modulus for the chosen G5F0.5 blend is not stated as a single number.
formulations.name: 5% GelMA + 0.5% fibrinogen (G5F0.5)
formulations.cell_type: PC12 cells and glial cells in layers
formulations.key_outcome: 10 µm cross-layer fibres guided neurite direction; glial layers promoted PC12 migration.

evidence.quote: a concentration of 5 % GelMA and 0.5 % Fib was selected as the matrix material for constructing the biomimetic cortical model in this study
the compression modulus of the G5 group (8.48 kPa) was closer to the modulus of natural cortical tissue
glial cells significantly promoted the migration of surrounding PC12 cells towards the glial layer but did not contribute to the extension of neurites
